finding.claim: validateFileName calls .toLowerCase() on a non-string LOAD DATA parameter when a malicious server sends a LOCAL INFILE request, throwing a TypeError that escapes the socket data handler and can crash the process (availability only).
finding.source: Server-sent LOCAL INFILE request packet (lib/cmd/parser.js:759 readStringRemaining) with permitLocalInfile enabled and app query LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE ? whose first parameter is non-string (undefined, null, number, Buffer).
finding.sink: parameters[0].toLowerCase() at lib/misc/parse.js:426 (and parameters.toLowerCase() at :428 for non-array values).

trace.note: socket 'data' listener bound directly to streamIn.onData, no try/catch
second branch taken: sql matches LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE ? and parameters.length > 0

finding.guards_checked: permitLocalInfile gate (parser.js:742; default false, connection-options.js:158) passes only when opted in; first regex branch (parse.js:410-416) does not match because SQL contains '?'; no type guard on parameters; filename regex escaping (parse.js:408) does not run on this branch; infileStreamFactory not reached. Confidence: plausible, code-path confirmed by reading, not reproduced.

finding.claim: String escape mode is read from this.info.status at write time; if a session sql_mode change to NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES is in flight on a pipelined connection, a parameterized value is backslash-escaped while the server parses it in no-backslash mode, allowing a quote breakout. Unverified: whether info.status updates only on response.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled string passed as a ? parameter value (e.g. from an HTTP request) on a connection where the application itself issues SET sql_mode = ...NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES pipelined before the query.
finding.sink: Literal written with backslash escaping by writeDefaultStringEscapeQuote / writeUtf8StringEscapeQuote, selected via noBackslashEscapes() at lib/io/packet-output-stream.js:383 and :549-553; invoked from lib/cmd/query.js:94-95.

trace.note: noBackslashEscapes() reads this.info.status at write time
writeDefaultStringEscapeQuote selects CHARS (backslash) vs QUOTE (doubling) regex by mode
parallel escapeString path (Utils.escape) uses same info.status check

finding.guards_checked: Mode-aware escaping from server status; pipelining enabled only when permitLocalInfile is false (connection-options.js:158-159). Attacker cannot trigger the mode change; requires the application to issue it on the same connection while the query is in flight. Confidence: low, unverified.
